sections.content: Savannah, Georgia has quietly become one of the Southeast's most compelling real estate markets. With its historic charm, booming short-term rental scene, and a growing port economy, investors are paying close attention — and for good reason. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started (check out this guide on [real estate investing for beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) if you're new to the game), finding real estate deals in Savannah GA can be a smart move in 2024 and beyond.
Savannah GA Real Estate Market Overview

Savannah sits in Chatham County on Georgia's Atlantic coast, and its real estate market reflects a unique blend of influences. The city is home to the Port of Savannah — one of the busiest ports in the United States — which drives consistent job growth and housing demand. Add in the Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD) with over 15,000 students, a booming tourism industry, and a growing remote-worker population, and you have multiple demand drivers that keep the housing market active year-round.

As of late 2024, the median home price in Savannah is approximately $285,000 — still well below national averages for comparable coastal cities. That said, prices have risen roughly 18% over the past three years, which signals strong appreciation potential. Inventory remains tight, hovering around 2.1 months of supply, which creates urgency for buyers and competitive conditions that wholesalers and value-add investors can leverage effectively.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Savannah

Not every ZIP code in Savannah offers the same opportunity. Smart investors zero in on specific pockets where the numbers work. Here's a breakdown of neighborhoods worth watching on the [Savannah GA real estate market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/savannah-ga):
Historic District & Victorian District

These are Savannah's crown jewels — beautiful antebellum homes with massive short-term rental upside. Airbnb properties in the Historic District routinely gross $4,000 to $8,000 per month. Entry prices are higher here, typically $400,000 to $700,000, but the cash-on-cash returns can justify the investment if you find a distressed property with cosmetic upside.
Midtown Savannah

Midtown offers a sweet spot for buy-and-hold investors. Median prices range from $180,000 to $260,000, and long-term rental demand is strong thanks to proximity to SCAD, major employers, and healthcare facilities. Three-bedroom homes here rent for $1,400 to $1,900 per month, producing solid cash flow at today's prices.
Eastside & Cuyler-Brownsville

These emerging neighborhoods are where wholesalers and flippers are finding some of the best spreads. Home values are appreciating as the neighborhood gentrifies, and distressed properties can still be acquired in the $80,000 to $140,000 range with ARVs pushing $200,000 to $240,000 after renovation. These deals require thorough due diligence, but the margins are real.
Pooler & West Chatham County

Pooler is one of the fastest-growing suburban markets in Georgia. Located near the airport and several major distribution centers, it attracts working families and logistics employees. New construction dominates here, but savvy investors are finding value-add opportunities in older subdivisions priced between $200,000 and $280,000.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Savannah
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Savannah, particularly in transitional neighborhoods like Cuyler-Brownsville and parts of Eastside. Assignment fees of $8,000 to $20,000 are common on deals where motivated sellers need a fast exit — think probate situations, absentee landlords, and pre-foreclosure homeowners. If you're newer to this strategy, our [guide on wholesaling real estate for beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) is a great starting point before you hit the market.
Fix and Flip

Flippers are finding consistent opportunities in Savannah's older housing stock. The city has thousands of homes built between 1940 and 1980 that need updating — kitchens, baths, roofs, and HVAC systems. A well-executed flip in Midtown or Eastside can generate $35,000 to $65,000 in profit. Always run your numbers carefully before committing. Use the free [ARV Calculator at aiwholesail.com](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate after-repair value quickly and accurately.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

Long-term rentals are a natural fit given Savannah's strong tenant pool. Vacancy rates in the city sit around 5%, and rent growth has averaged 6% annually over the past four years. Short-term rentals (STRs) in the Historic District are especially lucrative, though the city does regulate STR permits, so check current rules with the City of Savannah before purchasing.

Input your purchase price, estimated rehab costs, and expected ARV to instantly see your Maximum Allowable Offer (MAO) — this keeps your numbers honest and your offers competitive.
Key Market Trends Shaping Savannah Real Estate in 2024

items: Port Expansion: The Port of Savannah is undergoing a $1 billion infrastructure expansion, expected to add thousands of jobs and increase housing demand in surrounding areas through 2026.

Remote Worker Migration: Savannah's quality of life and relatively low cost of living continues to attract remote workers from high-cost cities like New York and Boston, pushing up demand for single-family rentals.

Tourism Growth: Visitor numbers to Savannah hit record highs in 2023, with over 15 million annual visitors. This sustains the short-term rental market and keeps hospitality-adjacent real estate values strong.

Rising Insurance Costs: Coastal proximity means flood and wind insurance costs are climbing. Budget $2,000 to $4,500 annually for insurance on investment properties — a number that materially affects your cash flow projections.
Interest Rate Pressure: Higher rates have pushed some local buyers to the sidelines, which has created more motivated sellers and better entry points for cash or hard-money buyers.

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Deals in Savannah

The best real estate deals in Savannah GA rarely hit the MLS. Off-market sourcing is where serious investors gain their edge. Strategies like driving for dollars in transitional neighborhoods, pulling absentee owner lists, targeting probate court filings, and building relationships with local attorneys and wholesalers all produce results. For a deep dive into these tactics, read our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) — it covers every sourcing channel with step-by-step instructions.

Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Savannah

Savannah attracts significant investor interest from out of state, particularly from investors in New York, California, and the Midwest looking for better cap rates and lower entry prices. But investing remotely requires preparation. Here's how to approach it the right way, and remember to [analyze your deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) before committing any capital.

items: Build a local team first: Find a reliable property manager, a licensed contractor with investment property experience, and a local real estate attorney before you buy. These relationships are your foundation.

Understand flood zone designations: Many Savannah properties fall within FEMA flood zones. Always check flood zone status and get insurance quotes before making an offer — Zone AE properties carry mandatory flood insurance requirements that can add $1,500 to $3,000 annually.

Visit at least once: Even in a data-driven market, walking a neighborhood tells you things that no spreadsheet can. Plan at least one due diligence trip to assess condition, block quality, and rental comparables firsthand.

Use local comps, not national averages: Savannah's micro-markets vary block by block. The Historic District and Cuyler-Brownsville are worlds apart in pricing and tenant profiles. Rely on hyperlocal sold data from your agent or an AI-powered tool.

Account for short-term rental regulations: If you plan to run an Airbnb or VRBO, confirm the property is in a zone that allows STR permits. The City of Savannah limits the number of non-owner-occupied STR permits in certain historic zones.

Screen property managers carefully: Self-managing from out of state is extremely difficult. Interview at least three local property management companies, check their Google reviews, and ask for a sample monthly statement before signing any contract.

sections.content: Is Savannah GA Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Savannah offers something rare in today's market: multiple investment strategies that all work simultaneously. Wholesalers can find spread in emerging neighborhoods. Flippers have abundant aging housing stock to renovate. Buy-and-hold investors benefit from strong rental demand and steady appreciation. And short-term rental operators can generate outsized cash flow in the Historic District. The key is knowing which strategy fits your capital, risk tolerance, and bandwidth — then executing with discipline and accurate numbers.
